sectionsContent.title: Mole Conversions

concept.summary: A mole is a counting number, the way a dozen is: one mole is 6.022 × 10²³ of whatever you are counting. Molar mass is the bridge between a number you can count and a mass you can weigh — how many grams one mole weighs, read off the periodic table in g/mol.
keyIdeas: Grams and particles never convert directly. Every conversion goes through moles.
Molar mass of a compound is the sum over every atom in the formula — subscripts multiply.
Carry units through every step. If the units do not cancel to what you want, the setup is wrong, not the arithmetic.

priorKnowledge.label: BEFORE YOU START — YOU ALREADY KNOW THIS
items: Reading a formula: a subscript counts the atom just before it, and a subscript outside parentheses multiplies everything inside (U6).
Finding atomic mass on the periodic table — the decimal number, not the atomic number (U1 S1.5).
Scientific notation and significant figures (U7 S7.1).

sectionsContent.directions: Show every step in the box provided. Carry units the whole way through. Round only at the end, to the correct number of significant figures.

questions.prompt: Write the molar mass of each, to two decimal places. Show the sum, not just the answer.
Ca(NO₃)₂ — how many atoms of each element are in one formula unit? Then find its molar mass.
How many moles are in 45.0 g of NaCl?
What is the mass of 2.50 mol of CO₂?
Complete the conversion map. Write what belongs in the middle box, then label each arrow with the factor that makes that conversion.

diagram.label: COMPLETE THE MAP
diagram.caption: Grams and particles never touch. Every path runs through the middle.

questions.prompt: How many molecules are in 18.0 g of H₂O?
parts: This is two conversions, not one. Do them in order and do not skip the middle.

questions.prompt: A sample of oxygen gas occupies 11.2 L at STP. Find the mass of the sample.
A student weighs out 25.0 g of Ca(NO₃)₂ for a lab.
parts: a.  How many moles did they weigh out?
b.  How many nitrate ions are in the sample?
c.  The lab calls for 0.200 mol. Too much or too little, and by how many grams?
d.  Their partner says “just weigh 25 g, close enough.” Using your answer to c, say whether you agree and why.
